title: Negative information questions with singular olla forms
summary: In an ordinary negative information question, keep the question word first and use the negative verb: Miksi sinä et ole kotona? Miksi sinä et ole kotona? — Koska olen koulussa.
targetSkills: Negative information questions with singular olla forms
objectives: Build a singular negative information question with the appropriate negative verb and ole.
Supply the requested information instead of treating the question as yes/no.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns.
The inessive is the in-place form, answering where.
An adjective is a word that describes a quality.
A pronoun stands in place of a name or noun.

In an ordinary negative information question, keep the question word first and use the negative verb: Miksi sinä et ole kotona? (“Why aren't you at home?”). Singular forms are minä en ole, sinä et ole and hän ei ole. Ole stays unchanged after the negative verb.
keyPoints: Do not add -ko/-kö to the negative verb in these ordinary question-word questions.

sections.title: Answering the question
paragraphs: The answer supplies the requested information. A negative question does not require a negative answer: Miksi et ole kotona? can receive Koska olen koulussa (“Because I am at school”). When confirming an excluded place in a bounded comparison, En ole koulussa means I am not at school. Read the intended reply before choosing its form.
A natural short reply to “Miksi sinä et ole kotona?” is “Koska olen koulussa.” (“Because I am at school.”). Use the full reply when it makes the person, action or correction clearer.
The exercises show supporting Finnish words and their meanings when recalling them is not the task. Read the complete English meaning before choosing the question or answer form.
keyPoints: The negative verb agrees with the reply's person and is followed by ole, not olen or on.

sections.title: Build the answer forms
paragraphs: Olen means I am here. Olla has the I-form olen: ole- + -n. The ending identifies the speaker.
on means is here. Olla has the irregular singular third-person form on.
en means I do not here. En is the first-person singular negative verb. The main verb takes its negative form.
ole means be here. After a present-tense negative verb, olla takes the unchanged form ole.
keyPoints: The negative verb agrees with the reply's person and is followed by ole, not olen or on.
